issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC and HAS_NAMED pre-filters derived from NUMERIC_TO_NAMED keys miss valid font-weight values outside 100..900 steps.
issues.detail: HAS_NUMERIC is built only from NUMERIC_TO_NAMED.keys() (100..900 by 100). A declaration like `font-weight: 550` will fail the pre-test and silently skip a value the rule used to flag. The fast-path duplicates the canonical keyword set and will drift. Use `/\d/` or derive the regex from the authoritative source.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks /i flag while sibling HAS_KEYWORD has it, creating asymmetric case-sensitivity rules.
issues.detail: HAS_KEYWORD uses `\b` and `/i`; HAS_PERCENTAGE uses `(?:^|[,\s])` and no flag. Keyframe selectors are ASCII so it works today, but the asymmetry is incidental complexity from copy-paste that will mislead a future maintainer. Pick one shape and document why.

issues.description: import-notation url() fast-path conflates textual appearance with semantic presence and may suppress diagnostics.
issues.detail: `/url\(/i.test(params)` matches inside comments or quoted strings like "url(", and the early return when primary === 'url' skips the parser path that could flag malformed url() or invalid string-form imports. Confirm no diagnostic is suppressed; otherwise the perf win comes at correctness cost.

issues.description: Pre-filter safety invariants are never stated in code or PR description.
issues.detail: Each filter implicitly claims 'any value that would trigger the rule passes this regex' but the invariant is undocumented. A one-line literate comment per filter ('safe over-approximation: any reportable value matches') would make these correct-by-inspection rather than correct-by-trust, and would help when future keywords are added.

issues.description: walkRules(/:/) and /(?:min|max)-/i filters over-match and provide minimal pre-filtering value.
issues.detail: Nearly every selector contains a colon (pseudo-classes, attribute values), so `/:/` is essentially a no-op on real stylesheets. Similarly `(?:min|max)-` matches innocent substrings. Acceptable as coarse pre-filters since the real parse runs after, but the perf gain is small — tighten to `/::?[a-z]/i` or add a comment naming them coarse filters.

issues.description: Performance claim is asserted without benchmark evidence.
issues.detail: The change is plausibly faster by skipping parseSelector/valueParser on inputs that cannot trigger reports, but no profile, no before/after timings on a representative corpus is included. The deeper question — why parseSelector and valueParser are slow on trivial input — is being answered by scattering guards across five files rather than fixing cost at the source.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a NEEDS-WORK PR: the right shape (cheap pre-filters before expensive parsing) but with two real correctness risks. HAS_NUMERIC in font-weight-notation silently skips valid non-canonical weights like 550, and the import-notation url() short-circuit substitutes textual appearance for token identity, potentially suppressing diagnostics. The HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD case-sensitivity asymmetry is a copy-paste hazard. Throughout, the pre-filter safety invariants are undocumented and the performance claim is unmeasured — fix the two correctness issues, tighten the asymmetric regexes, add literate comments, and show benchmark numbers.
